name: rtk (Rust Token Killer)
mechanism: Single Rust binary CLI proxy; per-command filters (filter, group, truncate, dedupe) on shell command output before it reaches context; 100+ commands; bytes/4 token estimate; rtk gain stats
claimed_saving: 60-90% of LLM tokens on common dev commands (vendor); ~118K -> 24K on a medium TS/Rust session (vendor table); per-command ~70% file reads to ~90% test runs
hooks_in_how: Claude Code PreToolUse hook (native binary) that rewrites Bash commands (e.g. git status -> rtk git status); fires only on Bash, so native Read/Grep/Glob/Edit bypass it; rtk bypass <cmd> runs one command unfiltered
risk: Independent Quesma Terminal-Bench 2.1 run (1,740 attempts, >$1,500): token savings did not lower cost; DeepSeek cost +17%, Fable ~flat; pass rates slightly down; extra turns cancel savings (https://zeli.app/story/49656471 and https://braindetox.kr/en/posts/rtk_terminal_compression_cost_benchmark.html, secondary reports of the Quesma post). gain metric counts removed output not money; discover overstates (issue #538 https://www.goodfirstissue.org/rtk-ai/rtk/issues/538). Many mirror forks exist (chelout, Anyesh, etc.) - use rtk-ai upstream. Failure full-log behavior undocumented on page.

name: context-mode
mechanism: MCP server + hooks: sandboxes tool output (ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file, ctx_batch_execute, ctx_index, ctx_search, ctx_fetch_and_index) so raw payloads stay out of context; only stdout enters context; SQLite FTS5 + BM25 session memory that survives compaction
claimed_saving: 98% (315 KB -> 5.4 KB across 14 scenarios); ctx_execute 56 KB -> 299 B; ctx_execute_file 45 KB -> 155 B; 47x Read 700 KB -> 1x ctx_execute 3.6 KB; ctx_batch_execute 986 KB -> 62 KB (all vendor README)
hooks_in_how: Plugin registers 6 hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, SessionStart, Stop) and 11 MCP tools; PreToolUse redirects or blocks dangerous calls to the sandbox; SessionStart injects routing instructions; /context-mode:cm-stats shows per-tool savings
risk: Savings are self-reported (BENCHMARK.md test method not read); fixes per-call size, not cross-source questions (third-party review via https://getunblocked.com/blog/sandboxing-mcp-output-vs-context-engine/); agents must actually route through sandbox tools (instruction compliance ~60% on hookless IDEs); license NOASSERTION - check before use; Node >=22.5 on Linux; other clients partial

name: codebase-memory-mcp
mechanism: Single static C binary; tree-sitter (162 languages) builds persistent SQLite knowledge graph of functions, classes, imports, routes; read-only openCypher subset, BM25 and optional semantic search; hybrid LSP type resolution for 10 languages
claimed_saving: 99.2% (about 3,400 vs 412,000 tokens, 5 structural queries vs file-by-file grep; ~120x) vendor single scenario; arXiv 31-repo study 10x fewer tokens, 2.1x fewer tool calls, answer quality 83% vs 92% for file-by-file (cited on project page)
hooks_in_how: Installer writes MCP entry to ~/.claude.json; also ships skill and Scout/Verify/Auditor agents; hooks are context-only and fail-open: SessionStart/SubagentStart add session context, PreToolUse on Grep/Glob/Bash adds matching graph symbols, PostToolUse on Read adds coverage notes; never blocks or replaces a tool call
risk: Baseline is naive grep, not optimized search; no reproducible harness published (Agentic Context Research replication flagged this, search summary https://letsdatascience.com/news/codebase-memory-mcp-speeds-ai-coding-agent-queries-a6a04a1b); answer quality drops 9 points in the arXiv study; graph tools do not uniformly win (code-review-graph ~5% on one task per Ubuntu benchmark summary); the 99% figure is a best case

name: serena (oraios)
mechanism: MCP toolkit with LSP-backed symbol tools (find symbol, references, symbolic edit) so the agent reads symbol bodies rather than whole files; license NOASSERTION
claimed_saving: No published before/after token benchmark found in this pass. Third-party only: serena-slim reports 50.3% fewer schema tokens (29 tools -> 18), measured with tiktoken; an install guide claims 70% fewer tokens vs whole-file reads (no method)
hooks_in_how: MCP server only (no Claude Code hooks found in this pass); tool schemas deferred by Claude Code tool-search by default, so tool count matters for overhead
risk: Savings unmeasured by the project itself; tool-schema overhead can exceed savings on small tasks; LSP setup per language; license NOASSERTION - check

name: token-savior
mechanism: MCP server for structural code navigation plus persistent memory engine; optional PreToolUse Bash rewriter and PostToolUse compactors installed via ts init --agent claude
claimed_saving: Headline (unverified, harness unpublished): 78.3% -> 97.9% pass, -80% active tokens (17,221 -> 3,395), -83% wall time; re-run 2026-10-07 on 8 tasks x3 passes, Haiku 4.5: cost -45% ($0.226 -> $0.123), new tokens -59%, wall time +40%
hooks_in_how: MCP core with alwaysLoad true needed on Claude Code 2.1.28x+ or tools hide behind ToolSearch; optional hooks by env var: TS_BASH_REWRITE=1 (PreToolUse, edits commands before run), TS_BASH_COMPACT=1 (PostToolUse, does not shrink current turn), SessionStart memory hook; merged into ~/.claude/settings.json
risk: Headline benchmark repo returns 404; withdrawn 2026-08-09 run where only 1 of 143 sessions called a TS tool; wall time worse in re-run; editing gains noisy (-54% to +16%); claude -p inherits settings.json so hooks contaminate control arm; small sample; young project (1.2k stars)

name: chop
mechanism: Go CLI output compressor; wraps Bash commands (chop git status); 52+ command filters plus auto-detect for JSON, CSV, tables, log lines; chop gain tracks savings locally
claimed_saving: 50-90% by category (vendor ranges); examples git status 247 -> 12 tokens (~95%), docker ps 850+ -> ~250 (~70%), npm test 1,200+ -> 5 (~99%); no measurement method stated
hooks_in_how: chop init --global registers a PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash in ~/.claude/settings.json; chop init --status, chop doctor, chop hook-audit verify; chop disable bypasses globally
risk: Very new, 46 stars, unverified numbers; hook rewrites can be dropped on Claude Code <2.1.168 when other Bash PreToolUse hooks exist; breaks if binary path moves; git diff compressed by default and breaks interactive use; failure full-output behavior not documented; same wrapped-output cost caveat as rtk (fewer tokens does not mean fewer turns)

name: repomix
mechanism: Packs a repo into one AI-friendly file (XML/markdown/plain), with token counting and a compress option (tree-sitter signatures) for whole-repo context; a packer, not a per-call filter
claimed_saving: None measured in this pass; project markets single-file packing for LLMs
hooks_in_how: CLI and MCP; no Claude Code PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook found; used by the user or agent on demand, so saving depends on what is packed
risk: Whole-repo pack can be much larger than what a task needs (wrong tool for targeted lookup); no before/after evidence found; token counts depend on tokenizer

name: ast-grep
mechanism: Rust CLI for structural (AST) code search, lint and rewrite; returns matched nodes rather than raw grep lines; MCP wrapper exists separately
claimed_saving: None published by the project for token use; saving would come from precise matches replacing grep-then-read loops (not measured in this pass)
hooks_in_how: CLI invoked by the agent via Bash (so an output-filter hook would see it); no Claude Code hook built in; MCP server is a separate project
risk: Pattern-writing overhead and syntax-per-language; no token benchmark found; not a compressor by itself
